name: Low Earth Orbit (LEO 400 km)
description: Standard low-inclination orbit. High revisit frequency over populated latitudes, short orbital period with frequent 36-minute battery drain eclipses.

name: Sun-Synchronous Polar Orbit (SSO 700 km)
description: Precessing polar orbit where the satellite crosses the equator at the identical local solar time every day. Gold standard for optical Earth observation and climate tracking.

name: Geostationary Earth Orbit (GEO 35,786 km)
description: Synchronous orbit matching Earth's rotation. Satellite appears stationary over one hemisphere. Continuous ground station link, but requires heavy propulsion to reach and operates inside the harsh outer radiation belt.

name: Low Lunar Polar Orbit (100 km)
description: Flies directly over lunar north and south poles. Overflights of permanently shadowed craters (PSRs) for water-ice scouting, with periodic loss-of-signal (LOS) behind the lunar far side.

name: Sun-Earth Lagrange Point 2 (L2 Halo)
description: Located 1.5 million km behind Earth. Uninterrupted view of deep cosmos, zero planetary thermal radiation, and continuous solar illumination with no eclipses. Communicates via NASA Deep Space Network (DSN).

name: Mars Polar Science Orbit (380 km)
description: Near-polar Mars Reconnaissance trajectory flying over Valles Marineris, Jezero Crater, and seasonal polar ice caps. Solar flux drops to 43% of Earth nominal.

name: Venus Cloud-Top Polar Orbit (300 km)
description: Maps Venus volcanic highlands beneath opaque sulfuric acid clouds using Synthetic Aperture Radar while soaking in 191% solar irradiance.

name: Europa Icy Ocean Polar Orbit (200 km)
description: Orbits Jupiter's ocean moon inside fierce Jovian radiation belts at 5.2 AU (3.7% sunlight). Demands Rad-Hard avionics and RTG or Mega-Solar wings.

name: Titan Methane Sea Orbit (1,200 km)
description: Cruises above Saturn's hazy golden moon at 9.5 AU to sound Kraken Mare hydrocarbon seas. Sunlight is 1.1% of Earth — Pu-238 RTG power is vital.

name: 16 Psyche Metallic Asteroid Orbit (120 km)
description: Ultra-low microgravity rendezvous (81 m/s orbital speed!) around exposed iron-nickel protoplanet core 16 Psyche at 2.9 AU (12% solar flux).
